facts: Spring-water pool on the Gimnyeong Geo-Trail; about ten minutes on foot through village alleys toward Gimnyeong Beach.
The spring stays near 15C; it is submerged at high tide and reappears at low tide.
The two sections were formerly gender-separated outdoor baths, and visitors take photos at the basin edge.
Residents long drew water and cooled off here.
The official guide calls it an SNS hot place and advises shooting its clear water at low tide in direct sunlight.
A basin that collected local spring water in Cheongsu-dong, Gimnyeong-ri.
Listed as a natural-ecology tourist attraction, always open, with no parking.
Cheonggulmul is a stop on the Gimnyeong Gojangnan-gil barrier-free route.
The guide says some ground surfaces at Cheonggulmul need a companion's help, although much of the route is cement path.
The guide presents ocean views, village paths and photos as the visitor experience.

theme.mountain.rationale: It is a coastal spring and village Geo-Trail site, not a mountain visit.

theme.ocean.rationale: The spring emerges near the sea and the site is on a coastal Geo-Trail toward Gimnyeong Beach.

theme.activity.rationale: Walking the Geo-Trail and cooling off in the water are documented, but it is not a dedicated activity facility.

theme.culture_history.rationale: Official sources document longstanding local water use and former gender-separated outdoor bathing.

theme.theme_park.rationale: It is a natural spring and trail stop, with no theme-park facility evidence.

theme.cafe.rationale: The attraction itself is the spring basin; no official evidence makes a cafe the visit purpose.

theme.traditional_market.rationale: KTO classifies it as natural-ecology tourism, not a market.

theme.festival.rationale: It is an always-open natural attraction, not a festival venue.

environment.indoor_ratio.rationale: The basin and trail are outdoors.

environment.weather_sensitivity.rationale: This outdoor attraction is also tide-dependent, with the basin submerged at high tide.

style_evidence.restfulness.rationale: Official descriptions emphasize cooling off in the cold spring and sitting at its edge.

style_evidence.physical_ease.rationale: Access includes village walking; the city accessibility guide says the surface at Cheonggulmul can require a companion's help.

style_evidence.visit_duration_flexibilit.rationale: It is always open and supports a short trail/photo stop or lingering in the water, though tide timing affects the full experience.

style_evidence.scenic_value.rationale: Clear spring water, ocean views and coastal-village scenery are central in public tourism guides.

style_evidence.distinctiveness.rationale: A cool coastal spring collected in a circular divided basin and revealed by tide has distinct characteristics.

style_evidence.local_embeddedness.rationale: This is a Gimnyeong community water-and-bathing site directly embedded in the Gimnyeong Geo-Trail and Jeju coastal-spring culture.

style_evidence.landmark_significance.rationale: It is an official Geo-Trail stop and major village-route spring, but evidence does not establish island-wide flagship landmark status.

style_evidence.photo_value.rationale: Official guides explicitly recommend basin-edge photography and optimal low-tide sunlight for clear-water shots.

derived_style.discovery_explorer.hold_reason: The current derived rule has no place-specific input.
